results.title: Lead Software Engineer
results.description:
Alternative Payments is building the financial operating system for SMBs, consolidating the disconnected tech stack that holds service-based businesses back. Starting with MSPs, we’ve spent five years perfecting accounts receivable, and we’re now expanding into accounts payable, AI-powered analytics, and beyond. We’re at an inflection point: closing the loop on money movement and laying the foundation for a platform that will reshape how service businesses operate financially.

We’re growing fast, thinking big, and building a global team that wants to be part of something that lasts. We believe the best solutions come from diverse perspectives, deep collaboration, and a shared obsession with customer impact. If you’re energized by real problems, real customers, and real impact, we want to hear from you!

## **What We’re Looking For**

We’re looking for a **Lead Software Engineer** to help set the technical direction of Alti, our AI agent product. Alti launched in July 2026 and has moved past MVP. The next step is scaling it into a core product of our platform: more agents, more automated routines, and our own machine learning models alongside LLMs.

You’re a product engineer who has built AI features in production and can raise the bar for the whole squad. You’ll own technical decisions across Alti, define how we evaluate and monitor AI features, and become a reference for AI across our product teams. This is a technical leadership role, not a people management role.

**This is a remote position based in Brazil.**

## **What You’ll Do**

- Own the technical direction of Alti features, from conversational AI to agents and automated routines.
- Define the standards for LLM evaluation, prompt management, monitoring and observability.
- Lead the design of RAG pipelines and agent architectures, and make the trade-off calls.
- Drive the move from LLM-only features to proprietary ML models, including taking them to production with monitoring and continuous feedback.
- Identify new ML use cases across the AP platform (e.g., invoice payment prediction) and shape them with Product.
- Act as a reference for AI inside the product org: review designs, pair with engineers and share practices.
- Keep shipping hands-on: this role writes code every week.

## **What You’ll Bring**

- Strong experience as a software engineer, with a track record of owning technical decisions on product features end to end.
- Hands-on work on AI products in the last 12 months (LLMs, agents, AI features), with ownership of meaningful parts of the system.
- Experience with chatbots/conversational AI, RAG and LLM evaluation pipelines.
- Strong skills in at least one of Go, TypeScript/JavaScript or Python.
- Autonomy to define a process in a new area, not only execute one.
- A product mindset: you care about what gets delivered to users, not only the model.
- Comfort in a fast-paced environment where you own many parts of the delivery chain.
- Professional working proficiency in English.

## **Nice to Haves**

- Experience putting ML models into production with monitoring and feedback loops.
- AI monitoring and observability tooling.
- Prompt engineering experience.
- Autonomous or personal agents working across channels (Slack, Teams, WhatsApp).
- Background in fintech, payments or financial products.
- Experience at both an early-stage startup (Seed to Series B) and a larger tech company.

## **What We Offer**

- **Competitive salary** tailored to your experience, skills, and expertise.
- **The total compensation range for this role is** $100,000 - $120,000, plus equity. The range displayed on each job posting reflects the approximate total target compensation for the position. Within the range, individual pay is determined by factors including relevant skills, experience, and education/training.
- **Equity opportunities** so you can share in our growth and success.
- **Unlimited PTO** and flexibility when you need it the most.
- **Yearly learning & development stipend** to help you grow and do your best work.

## **Why Choose Alternative Payments?**

At Alternative Payments, you’ll do work that truly matters.

- Own your impact: Lead meaningful, high-impact projects and collaborative initiatives that are shaping the future of FinTech and redefining how businesses get paid.
- Collaborate: Work with a diverse, innovative team where every voice is heard and great ideas come from anywhere.
- Grow with us: Your career journey is top of mind. We prioritize internal growth and give you the space to shape your path based on your goals — whether that’s deepening your expertise in your domain or exploring something new.
- Thrive in a supportive culture: As a scaling start-up, there’s a lot to be done and initiative is key. We believe in shared learning, open communication, and building each other up. When one of us grows, we all do.

***Want to see what we're actually building?***

We made a short video so you don't have to take our word for it. Get a glimpse of our product, our people, and the problems we're solving, then decide if it sounds like your kind of place.

## **Our Values**

- **Transparency & Honesty:** We communicate openly and truthfully with partners, investors, and each other so everyone understands where we stand and where we’re headed.
- **Resourcefulness & AI:** We stay scrappy, find creative solutions, and make progress even when the path isn’t obvious. We have a bias for action and seek out the information and resources necessary to make decisions and move quickly.
- **Partnership:** We win and lose together. We collaborate with our partners, investors, and teammates to tackle big challenges and reach shared goals.
- **Revolutionary & Boldness:** We challenge conventions, take calculated risks, and build better, stronger solutions that move our business and the industry forward.
- **Accountability:** We take ownership of our decisions and results. We follow through on our commitments knowing our work directly impacts our partners, our team and our business.

## **Applying to Alternative Payments**

We’re looking for candidates who are ready to step in and make an impact from day one. We know that sometimes people hold back unless they meet every requirement, but if you’re excited about the role, bring relevant experience, and are ready to contribute, we want to hear from you!

All resumes are reviewed by our small but mighty talent team. While we may use AI tools to help prioritize applications, real people are behind every resume review and hiring decision. We’re also committed to an inclusive and accessible process. If you need any accommodations during your application or interview experience, please let us know — we’re happy to help.

results.title: Staff Software Engineer, Product
results.location: Rio de Janeiro, São Paulo, Florianópolis, Curitiba, Belo Horizonte, Brazil, Remote
results.description:
**About LawnStarter**

LawnStarter is the nation's leading on-demand marketplace for lawn care and outdoor services, with over $150M in annual bookings. We're expanding beyond lawn care to become the one-stop shop for all home services — operating across three brands (LawnStarter, Lawn Love, Home Gnome) on a single shared platform.

**About Engineering at LawnStarter**

We build in small, focused initiative teams: a Product Engineer working alongside a PM and a designer, supported by an Engineering Manager who helps you grow. You'll also work shoulder-to-shoulder with engineering peers across initiatives in a shared codebase. The whole team owns whether the work moves its metric.

AI coding agents are a force multiplier here — they give a small, senior team the leverage to ship more, faster, and at a higher bar for quality. We hire engineers who are wired for ownership and energized by shipping to a real marketplace with customers and pros on both sides.

**The Role**

You're the engineering anchor of an initiative — working as part of a tight team with your PM and designer, and alongside engineering peers on adjacent initiatives. You have a hand in the full lifecycle: shaping the problem, deciding the technical approach, directing AI agents to implement much of the code, shipping to production, and — with your team — owning the outcome.

You're measured by impact, not by lines of code merged. When an agent can ship something safely, your job is to make sure it's done right and the metric moves. When the work touches a sensitive area, you have the guardrails to prove the change does exactly what it should, with no side effects: strong tests, evals, staged rollouts, and review gates.

**What makes this role exciting:**

- **You ship end-to-end.** From problem-framing through production to the post-launch metric review — you see the whole arc and own the result with your team.
- **You work as a true product partner.** You sit at the table with PM and design, bringing engineering judgment to product calls and product sense to engineering calls.
- **You get real autonomy — with the right checkpoints.** You make most technical calls yourself, with architect review on significant architectural decisions and fast input from peers.
- **You operate at a staff bar.** You're trusted to make the call, ship the hard thing, and stand behind the outcome.

### What You'll Own

- **The technical approach** — architecture, data model, integration choices, rollout plan, observability, and rollback strategy for your initiative. You make most calls yourself and bring significant architectural decisions to architect review; you document them, and revisit if the data says you were wrong.
- **Implementation quality** — the prompts, guardrails, evals, tests, and review loop that let agents ship safe, correct, production-ready code. Most lines will be agent-authored, and you're accountable for them — held to the same standard as the rest of the team working in a shared codebase.
- **Cross-functional partnership** — daily working contact with your PM (scope, tradeoffs) and designer (UX decisions, in-tool prototyping), regular collaboration with engineering peers, and weekly check-ins with your EM.
- **The initiative outcome** — the metric the initiative was set up to move. With your PM, you present results 2–4 weeks post-launch and share the "did it work" answer.
- **A high bar for what ships** — production correctness, security, performance, observability, and the experience for customers and pros. Agents accelerate you; they don't lower the bar.

### Problems to Solve

**Leading AI agents at a staff-level quality bar** Most of the code on your initiative will be authored by AI agents. The craft is making them ship as if a senior engineer wrote it: prompts that encode our conventions, evals that catch issues before merge, tests that exercise the edges, observability that catches a regression before a customer does. How do you build a workflow that lets a small team ship far more than its size would suggest?

**Owning decisions with high autonomy** You have real latitude to make and document technical calls quickly — with architect review on the big architectural ones and peers to pressure-test your thinking. How do you move fast, keep your team aligned, and stay accountable to the outcome?

**Shipping outcomes, not features** Each initiative is measured by a metric — a conversion rate, a retention curve, a pro-funnel KPI, a unit-economics shift. You're accountable for the number alongside your team. How do you scope to actually move it, decide what *not* to build, and have the discipline to follow up 2–4 weeks after launch?

### What Success Looks Like (Year 1)

- **Initiative outcomes hit** — You've shipped 3–4 initiatives end-to-end, and at least two clearly moved their metric (with the post-launch review to prove it).
- **Agent workflow that travels** — The prompts, evals, and review loop you built are picked up by peers on other initiatives.
- **Faster cycle time** — Median time from problem-framing to first production rollout on your initiatives is meaningfully shorter.
- **Quality holds** — No customer- or pro-facing regression traceable to agent-authored code that slipped through your review.
- **Visible leverage** — Peers point to artifacts you left behind — runbooks, evals, agent workflows, post-launch write-ups — as references they use.

**Requirements**

### Who You Are

- **AI-native.** Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, or equivalent are how you ship today — daily, on production work. You have real opinions about prompts, evals, agent loops, and review workflows, and you've built a workflow where agents write all of the code while you steer, review, and verify.
- **Operating at a lead level.** Whatever your current title, you've been the person making the call, shipping the hard thing, and standing behind whether it worked.
- **Outcome-driven.** You measure your week in "did the metric move" and "did the experience get better." You read the post-launch dashboard and own the answer.
- **A strong horizontal partner.** You hold your own with a strong PM and designer, and you collaborate well with engineering peers in a shared codebase. You bring engineering judgment to product calls and product judgment to engineering calls.
- **Decisive and documented.** You make architecture, data-model, and rollout calls, write them down, get fast input, and move.
- **A force multiplier.** Your impact compounds beyond your own initiative because you leave reusable artifacts behind — agent workflows, evals, runbooks, post-launch reviews.
- **Customer- and pro-minded.** This is a real marketplace with real people on both sides, and you care about the outcomes for both.

### Good to Know

- **An individual-contributor role with room to grow.** People management sits with the EM — but the path into management is an open door for those who want it.
- **A product-engineering role, end-to-end.** You ship features that move metrics; platform and architecture work happen inside the initiative when the outcome needs them.
- **Hands-on, with a high quality bar.** Agents handle much of the implementation; you bring the judgment, design, safety, and accountability. The bar is high.
- **Shipping to a live marketplace.** With $150M+ in bookings, customers and pros use what you ship within the same week.

### Tech You'll Touch

- **AI agents** — Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, internal agent stack, MCP servers, evals tooling
- **Backend** — PHP/Laravel
- **Frontend** — TypeScript/React/React Native (customer & pro apps, web and mobile)
- **Data** — Redshift, dbt, Segment, Airflow
- **Infra** — AWS, Datadog, Sentry, GitHub Actions
- **Documentation & process** — Brain (Claude Code skills + docs repo), Confluence, Jira

You don't need every box checked. You need deep skill in at least one of our stacks plus credible production experience with AI coding agents.

**Benefits**

- Competitive salary of USD $85,000–$125,000 annual base
- Work from anywhere
- High ownership and autonomy
- Fast-moving team that loves to build, learn, and grow

results.title: Principal Quality Engineer
results.location: Rio de Janeiro, São Paulo, Florianópolis, Curitiba, Belo Horizonte, Brazil, Remote
results.description:
**About LawnStarter**

LawnStarter is the nation's leading on-demand marketplace for lawn care and related services, with over $150M in annual bookings. We're expanding beyond lawn care to become the one-stop shop for all home services.

**About Engineering Quality at LawnStarter**

Our QA team is growing, and we're investing real money in better test coverage. We already have shared quality standards and a QA squad that organizes itself horizontally across teams. What we don't have is someone dedicated to owning that vision: every QA is heads-down on their own team, so nobody has the room to drive the standards forward, unify how the squad works, or push the state of the art. That's the gap this role fills. It's not a nice-to-have we're adding because things are going well. It's the structure and leadership we need to make what we've already built actually compound.

**The Role**

You'll be LawnStarter's first Principal Quality Engineer, reporting directly to the Head of Engineering. We already have quality standards, working CI/CD gates, and AI tooling in the mix. Nobody owns the vision behind all of it, drives it forward, or leads the QA squad that keeps it running. You will.

This isn't a QA management job today. You won't spend your day approving tickets or chasing bug counts. You'll take ownership of the standards and tooling that already exist, work collaboratively with the QA squad to improve them, and keep pushing the state of quality engineering forward as the org grows. As the QA squad grows, this role could take on direct people management of QAs, so hiring, coaching, and performance management experience is a real plus even though it's not the day-one job.

You're not starting from zero, and you're not inheriting a mess either. That means the job isn't "invent a strategy nobody has thought about." It's "listen to the QAs who live in this every day, understand where the pain is, and lead them toward what's next." We need someone who reads where LawnStarter is today and builds from there, not someone who shows up with a favorite tool stack and a coverage number they picked before they met the team.

**What makes this role different:**

- You own and evolve the quality strategy together with the QA team, instead of building one in a vacuum or just executing someone else's.
- You have direct sponsorship from the Head of Engineering and the room to keep growing the AI-native tooling already in the mix.
- Your success is measured by how much better the whole engineering org's quality gets under your leadership, not by a headcount number.

**What You'll Own**

- **Strategy and vision**: The company-wide quality engineering roadmap, plus a quality accountability framework that spells out what engineers, EMs, and PMs each own at every stage of building software.
- **Test strategy across the stack**: Unit, component, contract, API, end-to-end, mobile, and non-functional testing (performance, load, accessibility), agreed with each team as their quality contract.
- **AI-native quality tooling**: AI agents and skills, including Claude Code style tooling, that any engineer can run on demand for test generation, code review, and quality guidance. You'll keep hunting for the next AI capability worth putting in front of the team.
- **CI/CD and test infrastructure**: Required checks, quality gates, E2E and visual regression pipelines, performance budgets, and the mobile test automation strategy across emulators and real device clouds. That includes deciding what actually needs to block a deploy versus what can run async, and keeping the pipeline itself fast.
- **Production quality signal**: Tying monitoring into incident response and building dashboards teams actually check, not ones that just exist.
- **Technical mentorship of the QA discipline**: QA engineers keep reporting to their own Engineering Managers today. You won't manage their day-to-day or their careers right now. You'll own the technical and craft side of QA org-wide, mentor QA engineers across every squad, and send your input to their EMs to feed performance reviews. That could change as the squad grows into a direct reporting line to this role.

**Problems to Solve**

**A solid quality bar with no one steering it.**

We already have shared standards, working quality gates, and AI tooling in the mix. What's missing is someone whose job is to look at all of it, decide what needs to improve next, and actually drive that improvement instead of it being everyone's part-time responsibility.

**A QA squad with no dedicated leadership.**

Our QAs already organize horizontally across teams, but every one of them is focused on their own team's work day to day. Nobody has the bandwidth to unify how they work, spread what's working on one team to the others, or represent their pain points where decisions get made. You'll give that squad the structure and leadership it's missing.

**Standards that need continuous R&D, not a rewrite.**

The foundation works. The risk is standing still while the org grows. You'll keep pushing the state of the art, testing new approaches and tools, and deciding what's worth rolling out broadly versus what stays an experiment.

**Quality work that's still someone's side project.**

Right now, improving quality practice competes with each QA's day-to-day team commitments. You'll make it someone's actual job to carry that forward, and get engineers, EMs, and PMs treating it as planned work instead of something squeezed in.

**What Success Looks Like (Year 1)**

- **A clear quality vision, owned and communicated**: Every product team can point to what "good" means for their testing and why, with you as the person who set that direction and keeps it current.
- **Measurable improvement on existing gates**: Flakiness, pipeline cost, and what runs sync versus async on core repositories are visibly better than when you started, not just maintained.
- **At least one new AI-native capability shipped**: You've pushed the existing AI tooling forward with something new, like an added test-generation flow or audit, that engineers actually reach for weekly.
- **A QA squad that feels led**: The QAs across teams can point to concrete ways their work, tools, or standards improved because someone was finally driving it.

**Requirements**

**Who You Are**

**AI-native, specifically for quality work.** You already use AI to generate tests, not just to autocomplete code. You've set up agentic tooling like Claude Code or MCP-based workflows so engineers can run on-demand test generation or code review against their own repos, and you keep experimenting with what AI can take off a team's plate next. This is unlikely to be a good fit if AI tools mostly make you nervous, or your use of them stops at your own personal productivity.

**A strategic thinker, not a tool zealot.** Give you a team's current maturity level, and you'll design the testing approach that fits where they are, not the one you used at your last job. You resist the urge to mandate a specific framework or a specific coverage number before you understand the context. Someone who shows up insisting "we need to hit 90% coverage" or "everyone must use Playwright" without first learning how the team works will struggle here.

**Deeply hands-on across the whole test pyramid.** You've built and maintained component, contract, API, E2E, and performance test suites yourself, not just reviewed slides about them. You're the person who steps in when the engineering team is blocked by the pipeline and can't ship. If your test automation experience stops at reading dashboards other people built, this role will feel out of reach fast.

**A patient teacher who still ships.** Coaching engineers on testing practice and running enablement sessions is part of the job. So is personally building the CI pipelines and the tooling. You don't write the doc and hope someone else implements it. This is unlikely to be a good fit for someone who only wants to advise, or who avoids hands-on infrastructure work.

**Comfortable owning influence without owning headcount, at least for now.** You'll mentor QA engineers across every squad on technical craft and send notes to their EMs for performance reviews. You won't be their manager on day one, and you won't set their career path. This works well if you're motivated by discipline-wide technical influence. It won't if you need direct reports from the start to feel engaged. If you've hired, coached, and managed performance for a QA or engineering team before, that's a genuine plus: this role could grow into managing the QA squad directly as it scales.

**This Role Is NOT**

- **A traditional QA management job, at least not on day one**: You won't manage QA engineers day to day or own their career growth right now. Their EMs do that. You own the technical and strategic direction of the QA discipline instead, with the door open to direct management as the squad grows.
- **A "throw out what's there and start over" job**: We have real standards and tooling worth building on. You can't parachute in with a pre-packaged process or a favorite tool stack and mandate it regardless of fit.
- **A ticket-approval or gatekeeping role**: You're not the last line of defense that blocks releases at the end. You're embedding quality earlier, so there's less to block.
- **A headcount-growth play**: Your success isn't measured by how big a QA team you build. It's measured by how much better the whole engineering org's quality gets.

**Benefits**

**Compensation & Benefits**

- **Base salary**: $80,000–$100,000 USD annually.
- **Fully remote:** This is deep-focus analytical work with US-facing partners. We hire the best analyst regardless of city and trust you to manage your environment and overlap hours.
- **Flexible PTO:** Measured on outcomes, not hours logged.

*LawnStarter provides equal employment opportunities (EEO) to all employees and applicants for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age, disability, or genetics. We comply with applicable state and local laws governing nondiscrimination in employment.*

results.title: Senior Engineer (AI / Robotics / R&D), In-Home Care AI
results.description:
## Senior Engineer (AI / Robotics / R&D), In-Home Care AI

About Sierra Studio

Sierra Studio is an AI engineering and talent company that partners with a small, highly vetted group of growing companies. We run the hiring process on behalf of our partners, so when you apply through Sierra you get a direct line to the team and a process that respects your time.

Location: On-site, Culver City, CA

Compensation: $180k – $360k base, DOE, plus equity

Reports to: CEO

**About our hiring partner**

Our hiring partner is a mission-driven technology startup transforming the way in-home care is delivered through innovative AI solutions. Their platform unifies signals from cameras, sensors, wearables, and connected devices to turn raw data into secure, real-time insights and closed-loop care actions; giving families peace of mind, seniors dignified independence, and providers the tools to deliver safer, more proactive care.

They are a small, mission-driven team tackling one of the most important challenges of our time: helping people age safely and independently at home. If that excites you, they'd love to have you join them.

**About the Role**

Our hiring partner is hiring their first in-house engineer.

They want someone who can open the codebase, test ideas themselves, and get them real answers fast. Someone they can hand an open question to and get back working evidence, not an opinion.

Most of your week will be spent writing code: prototypes, integrations, internal tools, and R&D experiments. The rest goes to being the technical reference inside the company, the person their engineering partner syncs with and the person their CEO turns to when something needs a real answer.

A big part of the job is technical validation. They're constantly running into questions like: can we run this on-device? Is this open source speaker stack good enough? What would it take for a humanoid robot to do something actually useful in a home? You build the answer, bring back your findings, and you and the team decide together what makes it into the product. Turning a question into working evidence in days instead of quarters is the single biggest thing this hire unlocks.

This role is on-site at their office in Culver City, CA. You'll work in person with the team and hands-on with the hardware every day, especially as their robotics work ramps up.

As the team grows, this role is expected to evolve into technical leadership, with the opportunity to hire and lead other engineers. They're looking for someone who is a strong senior individual contributor now and wants that next step.

**What You'll Own**

Building

Write production and prototype code across the stack. This is a hands-on role, not a supervisory one.

Stand up MVPs and working demos fast, then validate them with real data or real users before committing engineering budget to them.

Build the internal tools and lightweight automation that let a small team punch above its weight.

Ship integrations with the devices, sensors, and third-party services our hiring partner depends on.

R&D and Technical Validation

Take open technical questions (new models, new hardware, new open source components) and turn them into working evidence.

Run experiments end to end: scope them, build them, measure the results, write up what you found, and recommend a call.

Experiment with robotics hands-on. They expect four to five humanoids on site, and someone needs to be in the room with them. Robotics experience is a strong plus, but curiosity and speed matter more.

Evaluate build vs. buy vs. integrate decisions, and be able to defend the answer.

Being the Technical Voice in the Room

Answer day-to-day technical questions from the CEO and the business side directly and plainly, without a translation layer.

Give leadership honest reads on feasibility, effort, and risk, so roadmap conversations are grounded in reality.

Push back on scope creep and unrealistic timelines when a project's ambitions outpace its resourcing, and say so early.

Support in building technical narratives for decks and funding rounds.

**Qualifications**

Required

5+ years building software professionally, with a track record of shipping things real people used.

Strong hands-on engineering skills. You write code every day and you're good at it: comfortable across the stack, deep somewhere.

Practical AI/ML fluency. You've built with LLMs, speech, or perception systems and understand where they break, not just how to call the API.

Experience taking a product from zero to a working first version, in an environment with incomplete information and no dedicated team.

Excellent written and verbal communication. You'll be the connective tissue between technical execution and business stakeholders who don't share your context by default.

Autonomy and ownership. No one is going to hand you a groomed backlog; you decide what matters this week and you're right about it most of the time.

Strong testing and QA discipline. You write solid tests, think through edge cases, and validate AI and hardware features before they reach users.

Based in the Los Angeles area (or willing to relocate), able to work on-site in Culver City, and authorized to work in the US without visa sponsorship.

**Preferred**

Experience with robotics, humanoids, embodied AI, or IoT and connected devices.

Comfort with hardware-adjacent work: edge deployment, audio pipelines, sensors, on-device inference.

Experience working alongside distributed engineering teams.

Early-stage startup background. You've been the person who did it all before there was a team.

Product instinct: you have opinions about what should be built, not only how.

Background in a technical discipline (CS, engineering) or equivalent self-taught technical depth.

**What Success Looks Like**

Open technical questions get answered in days with working prototypes, instead of lingering for a quarter.

Their engineering partner moves measurably faster because you're unblocking them and resolving unknowns ahead of their roadmap.

The robotics track has moved from interesting to demonstrable, because someone was hands-on with the hardware.

Leadership has a clear, current, evidence-based picture of what's technically possible and what it costs.

The CEO spends less time translating technology and more time on the business, because you're covering it.

You've laid the groundwork to bring on and lead additional engineers as the team grows.

**A Note on Fit**

This role suits someone who gets energy from variety and ambiguity, not someone who wants deep, singular focus on one system for years. We value curiosity, ownership, humility, speed, and thoughtful debate. Strong opinions are welcome, and they should be backed by evidence and a willingness to adapt. If your instinct when facing an unfamiliar problem is to go build something and find out, you'll like it here.

results.title: Technical Account Manager (AI Driven) - Curveglass
results.description:
Curveglass is a startup incubated by AE Studio that provides a flight-level correction layer for airline revenue management, helping airlines make better decisions through advanced data science and modeling.  
As part of the AE Studio ecosystem, Curveglass combines the speed, focus, and ownership of a startup with access to a broader network of engineering, AI, and product expertise.  
Curveglass runs directly inside each airline's cloud environment. Our product consists of a common **Core** and a client-specific **Adapter**, which handles everything needed to make Curveglass work within each airline's environment — including the web application, APIs, data integrations, business rules, and exports into the airline's systems.  
  
**ABOUT THE ROLE**    
  
As a Technical Account Manager at Curveglass, you'll own the technical implementation of Curveglass for airline clients end-to-end.  
This is a hands-on engineering role with broad ownership. You'll build and maintain client-specific Adapter code, work across frontend and backend systems, integrate with airline data and infrastructure, and deploy and operate Curveglass within client cloud environments.  
You'll also work directly with clients. That means understanding their technical and business needs, participating in and leading meetings, troubleshooting issues, analyzing recommendation results in collaboration with revenue management teams, and managing technical expectations as needed.  
You'll work closely with the Curveglass core team to determine what should be solved within a client's Adapter and what should become part of the shared Core. You'll bring client needs back to the team as roadmap input and Core change requests, while owning the implementation of client-specific functionality yourself.  
We're looking for someone who enjoys the full lifecycle of software engineering: understanding the problem, building the solution, deploying it, and seeing how it performs in the real world.  
You'll have meaningful ownership over the systems you build and the opportunity to influence Curveglass's architecture and product as we grow.  
If you enjoy owning technical problems end-to-end and working closely with the people using what you build, we'd love to talk.  
  
**ABOUT YOU**    
  
You're a strong, pragmatic engineer who enjoys owning systems beyond just writing the code.  
You're comfortable working across different parts of the stack and taking responsibility for an implementation from beginning to end: understanding requirements, designing the solution, building integrations and product functionality, deploying infrastructure, troubleshooting issues, and continuing to improve the system once it's live.  
You're comfortable operating in a startup environment where problems may not always come neatly defined. You can take ownership, make thoughtful tradeoffs, and move from an ambiguous problem to a reliable production solution.  
You also communicate well with people outside of engineering. You can understand the business context behind a technical request, explain technical decisions clearly, and lead conversations with clients when needed.  
You work well independently, collaborate closely with data science and product teams, and care about building software that is reliable, maintainable, and genuinely useful.  
  
**Required Skills and Experience**

- **Strong software engineering experience:** You can independently design, build, debug, and maintain production systems.
- **Fluency in Python:** You're highly proficient with Python and comfortable using it in production environments.
- **Full-stack development:** You're comfortable working with TypeScript and React and can own frontend functionality when needed.
- **SQL and data integration:** You can work confidently with relational data, APIs, client datasets, and production data flows.
- **Cloud infrastructure:** You're comfortable deploying and maintaining applications in AWS or Azure.
- **Containers and infrastructure as code:** You have hands-on experience with containers and tools such as Terraform.
- **End-to-end ownership:** You're comfortable taking responsibility for a system across application code, integrations, infrastructure, deployment, and ongoing maintenance.
- **Client-facing communication:** You're comfortable interacting directly with clients, leading technical meetings when needed, explaining decisions clearly, managing expectations, and pushing back thoughtfully when appropriate.
- **Business thinking:** You care about why something is being built and the outcome it needs to create, not just the technical implementation.
- **Production-minded development:** You write maintainable code and care about reliability, observability, debugging, and how systems behave in real-world environments.
- **AI-powered development:** You use modern AI coding tools as part of your daily development workflow and know how to use them effectively without sacrificing quality.
- **Self-management:** You can take ownership of complex problems, navigate ambiguity, and deliver without constant oversight.
- **Effective communication in English:** You're fluent in spoken and written English and can confidently communicate with both technical and non-technical stakeholders.
- **Timezone flexibility:** You're comfortable occasionally adapting meeting hours to work with clients across the Americas, Europe, and the Middle East.

**Bonus Points for**

- **Enterprise implementation experience:** You've implemented enterprise or data products where customers require meaningful integration and customization rather than a purely self-service SaaS product.
- **Airline or revenue management experience:** Familiarity with airline pricing, forecasting, revenue management, or related systems.
- **Data engineering experience:** You've worked with production data pipelines and technologies such as Parquet, Snowflake, or similar data infrastructure.
- **Spanish or Portuguese:** Professional proficiency in either language.
- **Startup experience:** You thrive in fast-moving environments, enjoy ambiguity, and are comfortable taking ownership beyond a narrowly defined job description.
- **Cloud deployment experience:** You've deployed and operated applications or infrastructure within enterprise AWS or Azure environments.
- **Strong product instincts:** You understand when something should be solved as client-specific functionality versus becoming part of a broader product.

**WHAT WE OFFER**

- **Startup environment, backed by AE Studio:** Join a focused, fast-moving startup while benefiting from the broader engineering, AI, and product ecosystem of AE Studio.
- **High-impact engineering:** Build production systems that directly shape the Curveglass product and how airlines use it.
- **End-to-end responsibility:** Own your work from architecture and implementation through deployment, integration, and ongoing operation.
- **Real-world problems:** Work on complex engineering and data problems within airline revenue management, where the software you build directly supports business decisions.
- **Direct product exposure:** Work closely with the people using what you build and bring those insights back into technical and product decisions.
- **Product influence:** Help shape Curveglass's architecture, roadmap, and approach to client-specific versus shared product functionality.
- **Small, collaborative team:** Work closely with engineering, data science, product, and leadership, with significant autonomy over how you solve problems.
- **Remote-first culture:** Work from anywhere, or connect with the broader AE Studio team and community.
- **Flexible schedules:** We care about outcomes, ownership, and impact—not micromanagement.
- **Competitive compensation:** Competitive pay and the opportunity to grow alongside the company.
- **Opportunities for growth:** Help shape how Curveglass approaches engineering, infrastructure, integrations, and technical decision-making as we scale.

Comprehensive medical, dental, and vision insurance for you and your dependents
Flexible PTO plus 14 company holidays
Paid parental leave


Annual learning and development stipend of $5000
Home office and commuter benefits

Technical screen (60 min) – practical coding exercise with an engineer.
Virtual onsite (3–4 hours) – coding, system design, a past-project deep dive, and a values conversation.
Final conversation – meet the hiring manager and team leadership.

# Software Engineer

## About Historiq

Historiq’s mission is to get history out of boxes and help cultural heritage professionals make a bigger impact at their organizations.

We work with archives, libraries, museums, and other organizations responsible for historical collections to bring more of their physical and digital materials into view. Our work combines archival expertise, digitization, and purpose-built technology to modernize how collections are arranged, described, managed, and discovered.

Historiq includes both archivist-led services and Historiq Una, our collections management platform. Across both, our goal is the same: help the people who care for collections work more effectively and make more history accessible.

## The role

As a Software Engineer at Historiq, you’ll help design and build the products and systems that support our platform.

The role spans frontend, backend, data, and infrastructure work. You may work on a web interface, add an API, improve a database-backed feature, or help build systems for collaboration, media processing, and digitization workflows.

You’ll work with experienced engineers, contribute to real product features, and take on more responsibility as you grow.

This role is intended for candidates with approximately 0–2 years of professional software engineering experience. Internships, research, open-source work, and substantial personal or academic projects can all be relevant experience.

## What you'll do

- Build and ship features across frontend and backend applications.
- Implement APIs, application logic, and database-backed functionality.
- Work with relational data models and database migrations.
- Build interfaces for digitization, archival processing, collaboration, and publishing.
- Help develop reliable file upload, synchronization, and media-processing workflows.
- Contribute to real-time and multi-user product experiences.
- Write unit, integration, and end-to-end tests.
- Debug issues across browsers, APIs, background jobs, databases, and cloud services.
- Participate in code reviews and technical discussions.
- Learn how applications are deployed, monitored, and operated in production.
- Improve documentation, developer tooling, and automated tests.
- Take ownership of increasingly complex features as you gain experience.

## Our technology

We work with a modern full-stack environment centered around Python, TypeScript, React, PostgreSQL, and cloud infrastructure.

Our systems include web applications, backend APIs, real-time communication, background processing, large-file and image workflows, desktop software, and AI-assisted document processing.

You are not expected to know all of these areas before joining.

## What we're looking for

- 0–2 years of professional software engineering experience, or equivalent experience through internships, research, open-source contributions, or substantial projects.
- Working knowledge of at least one general-purpose programming language
- Understanding of core software engineering concepts such as data structures, APIs, HTTP, and source control.
- Some experience building a web application, backend service, desktop application, or other non-trivial software project.
- Familiarity with relational databases and SQL.
- Experience using Git.
- An interest in writing well-tested, maintainable code.
- Ability to investigate problems and learn unfamiliar technologies.
- Clear written communication.
- Interest in working across different parts of a software system.

A computer science degree is not required. We care about what you can build, how you approach problems, and your ability to learn.

## Helpful experience

Any exposure to the following can be useful:

- Modern frontend development
- Backend APIs and web services
- Docker or cloud platforms.
- Automated testing
- Real-time applications
- Image, media, or file-processing software
- Desktop applications
- AI/LLM APIs, OCR, or computer vision


## How we work

We build iteratively and directly with the people who use our products, including archivists and other cultural heritage professionals. Their workflows and feedback shape what we build and how we improve it.

We work very collaboratively across a largely remote team, with cross-functional collaboration at every level of the company.

We care deeply about the problems we are solving and the impact we want to have: helping make more historical materials physically and digitally accessible much more quickly than ever before. We value accountability and teamwork in service of that mission.
